lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p20 - Point and say

details: Point and say activates vocabulary and prepares students for the story. Students identify the characters and the school rooms in the pictures before listening.
Look for correct pointing to the specific rooms (classroom, canteen, music room) and simple naming of the items.

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p20 - Listen to the conversation. Act it out

details: Listen and act develops narrative comprehension and speaking confidence. Students follow the story audio and then role-play the dialogue to practise the target sentence "We've got a...".

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p58 - Think about your school. Draw

details: Draw allows for personalization and creative expression. Students recall the rooms in their own school and draw a simple map or picture to represent them.
Look for recognizable drawings of different school areas (e.g., playground, classroom) reflecting the student’s actual school environment.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p58 - Look and tick

details: Look and tick reinforces vocabulary recognition. Students review the icons representing different school rooms and tick the ones that match their drawing or their actual school.
Look for accurate identification of the icons and logical ticking based on their drawing or school reality.

details: Talk about your school provides a fluency opportunity. Students present their work to a partner or the class, using the target structure "We've got..." to describe their school.
Look for confident speaking, correct use of the "We've got..." structure, and clear pronunciation of the room names.
